stories.title: The Big Four's AI squeeze
stories.summary: EY reported a 49 percent increase in AI services sales as the Big Four firms position the technology as a business transformation opportunity. They now face competition from their own partners, including Microsoft and OpenAI, which are bundling licences and implementation to undercut traditional consulting fees.

stories.title: Accenture managed services revenue overtakes consulting
stories.summary: Accenture revenue from managed services reached $37.3 billion in fiscal 2026, surpassing its $36.9 billion consulting arm. Managed services grew 8 percent year-over-year compared to 5 percent for consulting. It is the first time the company has reported this split since at least fiscal 2021.

stories.title: GPTZero identifies inaccuracies in Accenture research
stories.summary: GPTZero reported 31 inaccuracies across three Accenture research papers, including 15 in a single report on African development. The firm attributed the errors to human oversight rather than artificial intelligence. The report is currently being corrected for republication. Leapfrogging development apparently requires a functional spellcheck.

stories.title: KPMG Australia leadership reshuffle follows job cuts
stories.summary: KPMG Australia is eliminating 400 additional roles, bringing total recent job losses to nearly 800. The restructuring follows a confidential-information scandal that resulted in lost audit business and government contract restrictions. Chief executive John Sams has appointed three senior partners to new executive roles to stabilise operations.

stories.title: KPMG settles Silicon Valley Bank class-action lawsuit
stories.summary: KPMG agreed to a $224.5 million settlement regarding its audits of Silicon Valley Bank before the lender's 2023 collapse. The agreement, led by Norges Bank Investment Management and AP7, does not include an admission of wrongdoing. The firm had issued unqualified audit opinions since 1994.

stories.title: KPMG report finds leaders fear operational disruption
stories.summary: A KPMG report states 56 percent of global business leaders expect external disruptions to severely impact operations over the next three to five years. Some 70 percent of executives reported increased risk exposure over the past two years, citing geopolitical conflicts, energy shocks and climate-related events.

stories.title: EY report classifies AI adoption value
stories.summary: EY India reports that while AI adoption is broad, value remains uneven. Enterprises were categorised as Achievers, Challengers or Aspirants based on outcomes. Only 23 percent of respondents secured high value, while 44 percent reported low returns. The path to value realisation remains a work in progress.

stories.title: McKinsey warns of AI-driven cybersecurity threats
stories.summary: McKinsey reports that advanced AI has accelerated the exploitation of software vulnerabilities, with the window between disclosure and attack shrinking to hours. The firm recommends an overhaul of cybersecurity strategies, including higher investment in automated threat detection and continuous monitoring to manage the increased risk.

stories.title: Marsh acquires AltamarCAM to grow private markets
stories.summary: Marsh has completed its acquisition of AltamarCAM, a global private markets investment manager. The deal expands Marsh’s private markets assets under management to approximately $75 billion. The firm says the transaction strengthens its capabilities across private equity and real assets while establishing a larger international platform.

stories.title: Net at Work buys K&R Consulting Group
stories.summary: Net at Work has acquired K&R Consulting Group, a provider of Sage and Acumatica ERP solutions. The acquisition adds expert business consulting talent and market presence in key verticals for the technology advisor. K&R was founded more than 30 years ago by Brad and Dee Kain.

stories.title: Asper.ai acquires Pricing One assets
stories.summary: Asper.ai has acquired assets and talent from Geneva-based Pricing One to expand its agentic AI platform across Europe. The deal integrates a library of more than 650 commercial execution plans into the buyer's system. Asper.ai says the move combines its AI with Pricing One’s commercial strategy expertise.

stories.title: EXL acquires Aimpoint Digital
stories.summary: EXL has acquired data and AI consulting firm Aimpoint Digital, adding around 250 AI engineers and strategists to its workforce. The company says the acquisition will help enterprises move AI projects from pilot stages to production. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

stories.title: PwC acquires data boutique Datasparq
stories.summary: PwC UK has completed its acquisition of London-based Datasparq to strengthen services for private equity funds. The firm will integrate with the Value Creation unit of Strategy&. PwC says the move will help integrate new technologies into investment analysis, due diligence and post-acquisition value creation processes.

stories.title: RSK expands Australian rail capability
stories.summary: RSK has acquired BlueFin3 to expand its engineering and advisory presence in Australia. The firm says the acquisition brings together expertise in sectors central to the country's growth. BlueFin3 director Warren Burnett said the move provides greater scale while maintaining the consultancy’s existing culture and client focus.

stories.title: Onterris acquires EcOz Environmental Consultants
stories.summary: Onterris has acquired EcOz Environmental Consultants to expand its advisory services in Northern Australia. The company says it solves complex challenges for planet and progress. EcOz provides end-to-end environmental services and will be integrated into the company's consulting division to support regulatory and stakeholder risk management.

stories.title: Kaptio acquires Trawelt Consulting
stories.summary: Icelandic firm Kaptio has acquired Croatian company Trawelt Consulting. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: FICCI-EY report links 2 million deaths to air pollution
stories.summary: A report by FICCI and EY states that more than 20 lakh deaths in India were attributable to air pollution in 2023. The firms suggest treating worsening air quality as a public health emergency rather than solely an environmental concern. The knowledge paper was released by industry representatives.

stories.title: Government pushes for sustainable aviation fuel
stories.summary: The government is coordinating between the DGCA, NITI Aayog and FSSAI to promote sustainable aviation fuel. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Productivity cited as key to manufacturing growth
stories.summary: A recent article argues that India cannot become a manufacturing superpower without a productivity revolution. The author claims productivity is the real differentiator for innovation and market leadership. The piece suggests that becoming a leading manufacturing hub should be viewed as a national imperative rather than policy.

stories.title: Cabinet approves container manufacturing incentives
stories.summary: The Union cabinet has approved a Rs 10,000 crore incentive scheme for container manufacturing. The policy aims to reduce dependence on foreign suppliers after pandemic-era shortages disrupted trade. Manufacturers in Bhavnagar, Rajkot and Kutch are expected to benefit from the support for infrastructure and production costs.

stories.title: Passenger EV registrations jump 93.6 percent
stories.summary: Deloitte India reports that passenger vehicle wholesale volumes rose 30.7 percent in the second quarter of FY2027. Electric two-wheeler penetration crossed 11 percent, while passenger EV registrations jumped 93.6 percent. The report notes double-digit growth across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles during the period.

stories.title: EY-FICCI report calls for shipbuilding pipeline
stories.summary: A report by EY and FICCI states that India needs a predictable, long-term demand pipeline and better financing to grow its shipbuilding sector. India repaired 418 vessels in FY23-24, though its global market share remains limited. The authors suggest building an integrated and global shipbuilding industry.

stories.title: KPMG warns on private equity in healthcare
stories.summary: KPMG’s Alberto De Negri warns that private equity investment in India’s healthcare sector could increase treatment costs for patients. The firm suggests that without clear regulations and cooperation between public and private providers, the expectation of short-term returns may pose risks for the quality of healthcare.

stories.title: Bangladesh strikes offer opening for Indian exporters
stories.summary: Wage strikes at about 690 Bangladeshi garment factories have handed Indian exporters an opening in Western markets. Workers are demanding a monthly minimum wage of BDT30,000. While the government agreed to a new pay structure, the disruption occurred during the peak ordering season for Western retailers.

stories.title: Data centre boom faces local pushback
stories.summary: India’s data centre industry is facing local pushback regarding water and power usage. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Comparing ROI for Indian MBA programs
stories.summary: A comparison of IIMs and private MBA colleges highlights the importance of return on investment. Some top institutes charge fees exceeding INR 25 lakh, while others offer lower costs. Students are advised to consider future salary prospects against the initial investment required for management education.

stories.title: PhD graduates face a job paradox
stories.summary: A 29-year-old Chemistry PhD graduate from the Central University of Rajasthan is struggling to find work outside academia. He reports being overqualified for some roles and underqualified for others. Research and development openings in his specialisation remain limited. The degree has not yet provided a professional chapter.

stories.title: Bharti AXA Life Insurance appoints Sohan Tulpule to HR leadership role
stories.summary: Bharti AXA Life Insurance has appointed Sohan Tulpule as Head of Performance, Rewards, HR Operations and HR Technology. Tulpule joins from PwC India, following an eight-year tenure at KPMG India and a previous role at Deloitte. He brings nearly 15 years of consulting experience to the insurer.

stories.title: ABeam Consulting promotes Supreeda Jirawongsri to lead Thailand business
stories.summary: ABeam Consulting has appointed Supreeda Jirawongsri as Managing Director of its Thailand business, effective 1 April 2026. Jirawongsri, who previously served as Deputy Managing Director, brings nearly 30 years of experience in areas including corporate transformation, strategy and artificial intelligence. She will lead the firm's strategic direction.

stories.title: Uzzi & Lall appoints Rajiv Chandak as managing director for India
stories.summary: Uzzi & Lall has appointed Rajiv Chandak as Managing Director and Head of India. The full details of the appointment are available to subscribers of the source publication. The firm continues to expand its leadership team within the region.

stories.title: Knight Frank names new group strategy lead
stories.summary: Knight Frank has appointed Nick Lynch as partner and head of group strategy and executive office. Lynch joins from BT Group, bringing over 20 years of experience from roles at Bain & Company, Goldman Sachs and Deloitte. He will work with the leadership team to shape strategic priorities.

stories.title: Kate Espezel elevated to global head of executive leadership development at CHANEL
stories.summary: Kate Espezel has been appointed as Global Head of Executive Leadership Development at CHANEL. The full details regarding the scope of her new role and the company's leadership strategy are available to subscribers of the source publication.

stories.title: Sendero Consulting named a 2026 Top Workplaces D-FW winner
stories.summary: Sendero Consulting has been named to the Top Workplaces D-FW list by The Dallas Morning News for the fifth consecutive year. The award is based on an employee survey conducted by research partner Energage, which measures company leadership, compensation, training and flexibility. The firm remains on the list.

stories.title: Talenmark Corporation appoints head of corporate strategy
stories.summary: Talenmark Corporation has appointed Muhammed Hashir as Head of Corporate Strategy. Hashir will manage business performance across the company's hospitality, real estate, healthcare and infrastructure sectors. He brings over nine years of experience in management consulting and data-driven transformation to the Kerala-based firm.
